proof_nl:
Let n>1 be an integer and let t be a real number with 0<=t<1.

By the defining property of the floor function, floor(n t)=n-1 if and only if
n-1 <= n t < n.
So it remains to translate these inequalities into a condition on t.

First, if floor(n t)=n-1, then n-1 <= n t. Since n>0, dividing by n gives
(n-1)/n <= t.
Because t already satisfies t<1 by hypothesis, we obtain (n-1)/n <= t <1.

Conversely, if (n-1)/n <= t <1, then multiplying by the positive integer n yields
n-1 <= n t < n.
Applying the floor characterization again, this implies floor(n t)=n-1.

Thus, for every integer n>1 and every real t with 0<=t<1,
floor(n t)=n-1 if and only if (n-1)/n <= t <1.
solver_summary: Use the standard characterization floor(u)=m iff m<=u<m+1 with u=nt and m=n-1. The hypothesis 0<=t<1 makes the upper bound automatic after multiplying/dividing by positive n, giving the stated interval equivalence.
vetter_reason: The proof is a direct and correct application of the floor characterization: floor(n t)=n-1 iff n-1 <= n t < n, which is equivalent to (n-1)/n <= t < 1 for n>1. The argument is complete and matches the lemma exactly.
